question: Which declared ontology alternatives are reusable and structurally distinguishable on the fixed measurement bank before simulation?

alternative_definitions.hybrid: Fixed reusable-operation declaration with no interaction.
alternative_definitions.hybrid_plus_perfect_progressive_chain: The same hybrid plus the single declared optional interaction perfect_progressive_chain.
alternative_definitions.feature_only_control: One KC per observed schema dimension/value after excluding declared reference conditions.
alternative_definitions.exact_cell_diagnostic: One KC per exact canonical feature tuple; diagnostic rather than a reusable-skill claim.

kcs.name: perfect construction
kcs.description: Construct perfect HAVE and its participial dependency.
kcs.linguistic_rationale: Perfect and perfect-progressive constructions share the perfect HAVE relation; perfect-progressive is therefore compositionally activated.

kcs.name: progressive construction
kcs.description: Construct progressive BE and its -ing dependency.
kcs.linguistic_rationale: Progressive and perfect-progressive constructions share the progressive BE relation; perfect-progressive activates both aspect KCs.

kcs.name: canonical BE-passive
kcs.description: Construct passive BE and the lexical past participle.
kcs.linguistic_rationale: Canonical BE-passive adds an auxiliary-participle dependency and changes argument realization.

kcs.name: past finite-form selection
kcs.description: Select past finite morphology on the operator or main verb.
kcs.linguistic_rationale: Past is a reusable finite-form decision across aspect, voice, polarity, and clause type.

kcs.name: present finite-form selection
kcs.description: Select present finite morphology and agreement conditions.
kcs.linguistic_rationale: Present is a reusable finite-form decision across aspect, voice, polarity, and clause type.

kcs.name: imperative clause formation
kcs.description: Realize an English imperative main clause.
kcs.linguistic_rationale: Imperative formation is a reusable clause operation distinct from the declarative reference condition.

kcs.name: central modal WOULD
kcs.description: Select central modal WOULD and its base-form complement.
kcs.linguistic_rationale: The canonical schema distinguishes WOULD as a source-defined central-modal meaning/form choice reusable across compatible clauses.

kcs.name: verbal negation
kcs.description: Place NOT after the finite operator, inserting DO when needed.
kcs.linguistic_rationale: Negative polarity requires a reusable operator-placement decision.

kcs.name: polar-question formation
kcs.description: Form a yes/no question with finite-operator inversion.
kcs.linguistic_rationale: Polar questions require a reusable operator-subject ordering operation.
